subject: Recap: Software Factories, Measurement, and the Human Side
body:
Hey everyone,

Our latest 🦄 ai that works session dove into "The Software Factory Debate: Building, Measuring, and the Human Element"!

The full recording, code, and diagrams from the session are now available on GitHub:
https://github.com/hellovai/ai-that-works

We covered a lot on software factories, agentic coding, and the critical elements for their success. Here's a super quick recap:

*   **So, what exactly *is* a Software Factory?** We talked about it as an automated system, a sort of 'agentic loop,' that handles the whole software lifecycle. Imagine it taking an issue from creation all the way to launch, living in the cloud, and defined 'as code' so it's easy to measure and keep improving.
*   **Measuring Success Beyond PRs:** Forget just counting pull requests. Real productivity in these factories comes from tracking things like DORA metrics, cost per feature, and an 'automation index' (basically, how much human input each task still needs). Plus, using online evaluations helps turn good or bad runs into solid benchmarks for making our agents even smarter.
*   **The Human & Organizational Side:** Shifting from individual dev work to these public, 'multiplayer' factory systems isn't just a tech change. It's a big cultural one. We need to build environments where people feel safe to experiment (that's psychological safety!) and focus on managing risk in code reviews. This naturally leads to smaller, more focused pull requests, which is a win-win.

If there's one big takeaway from our discussion, it's this:
The real challenge with software factories isn't just the tech. It's almost always organizational. Companies often hit roadblocks because engineering and product teams work in separate silos. That makes it super tough to truly co-own the factory's output and optimize for shared customer outcomes.

Got questions? Just reply to this email, or even better, hop into our Discord: https://www.boundaryml.com/discord. We genuinely read every message and love hearing from you! Happy coding 🧑‍💻

Vaibhav & Dex
